steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: There are stark global inequalities in food consumption. The average daily calorie intake varies from over 3,700 kcal in the USA to under 2,100 kcal in countries like Burundi and Eritrea. The FAO recommends a minimum of approximately 2,350 kcal per day for a healthy active life.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: The Green Revolution (1960s-80s) introduced high-yielding crop varieties (HYVs), chemical fertilisers, pesticides, and irrigation to increase food production, particularly in Asia and Latin America.

steps.title: Key Contrast
steps.body: Subsistence farming produces enough food for the farmer's family with little surplus for sale. Commercial farming produces crops or livestock for sale at profit, usually on a large scale with modern inputs.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Sustainable food production means producing enough food for the current population without degrading the environment or compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use specific data (calorie figures, percentages) when describing global patterns For Green Revolution questions, give both sides - it increased production but also created problems Use named examples: India for Green Revolution, locusts in East Africa, France for food waste Higher mark questions need evaluation - consider whether strategies are truly sustainable Remember the difference between food insecurity (lack of reliable access) and famine (extreme shortage) Link food security to other topics: climate change, population, development, trade
